title: Zigarettenmarke "Egyptica" 20 Stück Blechpackung
desc: I. Kyriazi gründete, zusammen mit seinen Brüdern, 1873 in Cairo/Ägypten die Zigarettenfabrik Kyriazi Freres. Es wurden Unternehmen in Amsterdam und 1925 in Hamburg eröffnet. Nach dem 2. WK wurde eine Fabrik in Berlin gegründet. In den 1960er Jahren wurde Kyriazi von der BAT übernommen. Zwischen 1957-1972 wurde die Marke EGYPTICA in Berlin produziert. Unser Objekt ist eine leere 20er Blechpackung, etwa aus dem Jahr 1970. Neben dem Markennamen EGYPTICA ist auf dem Deckel noch der Firmenname mit Herkunftshinweis „Cairo (EGYPT)“ aufgedruckt. Auf der Rückseite findet sich ein Teil der Steuerbandrole, mit dem Aufdruck „Kyriazi –Berlin Packung 2,50 DM“, erhalten.

title: Blue glass bead with 'eye' decoration, T 051
desc: This bead is of truncated biconical shape and has a vertical perforation. It is made of semi opaque, wound, blue glass with an opaque creamy white horizontal trail, around centre of bead. The bead is decorated with 7 ‘eyes’ of which 4 are above and 3 are below the central divisional line. These 'eyes' are irregularly placed and comprise an irregular circle of opaque white with 2 inner concentric circles of yellow and white with a blue glass central dot. Beads decorated with ‘eyes’ of layered glass are known from many parts of the world including Egypt, Mesopotamia and Europe. Glass is an early form of synthetic material used in the formation of beads. The wound method refers to the manner of manipulation of the glass. Wound glass beads are among the earliest dated type of bead. Glass is heated to a workable state when it is wound around a form coated in a slip. While still hot the surface of the bead is decorated with rods of coloured glass or the rods may be built in during the winding process.

title: Assur archaeological site
desc: The ancient city of Assyria is one of the most important and famous monuments in ancient Mesopotamia. It is located on the west bank of the Tigris River in the district of Sharqat in Salahaddin province. Excavations in Assur began in 1900 by the Germans and more than 16,000 cuneiform tablets have been found, along with hundreds of other valuable objects, most of which are preserved in the German Museum in Pergamon. Since 1900, excavations have been carried out several times by other universities. The earliest recorded settlement dates back to the Sumerian period, and then occupied during the periods of Akkadian, Assyrian, Achaemenid and Parthian. The foundations of the temple of Ishtar are in this city along with many other palace foundations. The city’s golden age was the 9th-6th centuries BC when the Neo-Assyrian Empire ruled most of Mesopotamia, parts of Anatolia, parts of Egypt and even parts of Syria. The preserved remains of the city’s arched gate dates back to the 14th century BC.

title: Horus Falcon Figure in Bronze, MG 006
desc: This bronze statuette is of a standing falcon (H 19cm), the form in which the Egyptian God Horus was typically depicted. The eye sockets have been left hollow to allow for an inlay of precious stone or metal. The surface of the figure displays a type of decay typical of ancient bronzes: the piece would originally have been highly polished and possibly overlaid with precious metal. Horus, the son of Osiris and Isis, was primarily a sky god, though he often took on solar associations, particularly when merged with the sun god Ra. From the seventh century BC a vast number of bronze figurines of deities were produced in Egypt. More realistic statutory was common in the Late Period and fine metalwork used gold, silver and bronze. Mortuary ritual continued from previous generations. Excavations reveal that these figures were dedicated as votives at temple sites, including chapels above the galleries that contained sacred animal burials. Subterranean galleries packed with mummified falcons have been found at sites such as Saqqara. Festivals were a focal point and small artworks including metal statutory were central to celebrations.

title: Limestone Statue of a Baboon, MG 005
desc: This baboon (H19.5), of limestone, is seen squatting, forearms resting on its knees. A hole drilled into the crown of the head reveals that it was originally provided with a headdress. Other statuettes feature a combination of the sun disc and crescent moon, made of gilded wood. The Hamadryas baboon was typical of the New Kingdom distinguished by projecting whiskers and a thick shoulder mane. The smoothing of the face and shoulders of this statue reflects stylistic tendencies of the Late Period when other species of baboon were imported. Limestone statues were often brightly painted. The baboon was one of the manifestations of the god Thoth, an Egyptian moon deity, who was also depicted as an ibis-headed man. Thoth personified divine speech and was a god of writing, mathematics, astronomy and healing. Baboons were represented in the burial chamber of Tutankhamun and were common among the animal species excavated at the great animal necropolis in North Saqqara.

title: Egyptian Travertine, Cylindrical Jar, DG 100
desc: This travertine (Egyptian alabaster) jar (H 26 x W 16.5 x D 16.5cm) shows how the artist used skill and knowledge of the material to use the veins in the stone to create bands around the body of the vessel. The jar has a flared rim and stepped base and may at one time have been lidded. Travertine is found in small deposits across the Nile valley and in the Early Period was used in pavements and wall linings of temple passages. Travertine was also used in a wide range of canopic jars, statues, bowls and dishes. It is a dense, non-porous rock so suitable for use as ointment and oil containers. Common in ancient Egyptian items were travertine of translucent, coarse-grained type coloured in shades from pale brown to yellow tinged to orange with faint layering. A second type used was a banded calc-sinter (a freshwater calcium carbonate deposit). Travertine of darker colour fades to white on exposure to the sun.

title: Egyptian Head in Basalt, TB 003
desc: The lower half of a small head carved in basalt shows individual features suggesting a portrait. The top and back of the head have been completely removed. The left eye, except its lower frame and both ears are missing. The features are soft and rounded with quite a large round tipped nose and closed lips. On the base of what would have been the left ear is a protruding sub-square lobe of stone which may represent the remains of hair or a headdress. The base of the head is broken and badly abraded so it is difficult to assess whether this may once have been part of a larger figurative statue. It has been assigned a date in the Middle Kingdom and in particular the 11th or 12th dynasties.

title: Female figurine, JB 004
desc: This small wooden figure of a girl may be a funerary model, typical of Ancient Egypt. The figure, carved from a single piece of wood, is a naked female with underdeveloped features. She stands upright looking ahead with her arms by her sides. Her hands are not tightly fisted but her fingers are curved under and her thumbs are straight. She is reported to have been found in a boat. Her hair is short and curled. This may indicate her young status. As children Egyptians had shaved heads with just a single strand. As they aged girls grew their hair into a variety of styles. Hair decoration among women and girls used ribbons, flowers, rings and amulets. Women of early Ancient and the Middle Kingdom preferred short hair whereas later it became fashionable to have longer hair. The use of elaborately decorated hair and wigs was common among the elite and the royals. Wigs were often ‘helmet shaped’ and coloured, blue, red or green decorated with precious stones and jewellery. Braids and curls were added to wigs which grew larger over time. Small Egyptian figurines were used as models to produce larger sculptures, but could also be Ka statues. These, carved from wood or stone were painted and designed in likeness of their owner. Their purpose was to act as a receptacle for the ‘life-force’ or spirit of a body. This statue shows the rigid frontalism preferred, although the head is not turned, and may have stood in a small niche in a funerary house or mortuary chapel. Boats were significant in Egyptian religions, believed to be the travel method of the Gods. Small models of funerary boats, containing figurines represented the larger boats used to transfer bodies down the Nile to their places of rest.

title: Medieval Gilded Donkey Figurine, MG 139/025
desc: The domestic donkey has it’s origins in Egypt c. 4000 BC. They quickly became vital in the expansion of trade routes and from Africa their use spread from Syria to Siberia. The Roman Empire relied on the donkeys ability to act as pack animals and navigate routes such as the Silk Road from the second-century BC. Bridles and bridle bits were made of a wide variety of materials including wood, bone, horn, leather and rope. This donkey (H 8cm) is a gilded bronze figurine wearing a bridle of browband, noseband, cheek-strap and throat-strap. A hole in its back halfway between the shoulder blade and the hip suggests a removable saddle or pannier. A large area of the body, underneath the area covered by a saddle or pannier is no longer gilded but it is not clear if this is through wear. The four hooves are clearly defined and the long tail hangs straight down. The ears sit up straight and the mouth is clearly defined. Two opposing holes on either side of his mouth suggest a bit and reins may have been attached. The gilding is mostly present and in good condition although there are patches, including his tail which are worn.

title: Το βιβλίο της ζωής
desc: Από τις αρχές της δεκαετίας του 1970, ο Κωνσταντίνος Ξενάκης επικεντρώνεται σε μια σημειολογία τόσο της εικόνας όσο και της καθημερινής επικοινωνίας, προτάσσει οπτικούς κώδικες και δημιουργεί μία «γλώσσα» στην οποία στοιχεία από αλφάβητα διάφορων πολιτισμών συμβιώνουν με σήματα-σύμβολα της σύγχρονης πραγματικότητας. Ιερογλυφικά της αρχαίας Αιγύπτου ή τύποι της σφηνοειδούς γραφής, π.χ., συνδυάζονται με σημάνσεις οδικής κυκλοφορίας, ενώ τα αρχετυπικά σχήματα, τα πρωτογενή μοτίβα, οι σχέσεις σημαίνοντος και σημαινόμενου, η φιλοσοφική-συμβολική διάσταση, η διαχρονική και διαπολιτισμική προσέγγιση ορίζουν τον πυρήνα της δημιουργίας του, η οποία διατηρεί πάντα τον πρωτοποριακό και πειραματικό της χαρακτήρα.
credit: Metropolitan Organisation of Museums of Visual Arts of Thessaloniki – MOMus

title: End of an exhibition
desc: Visitors queue for the exhibition 5000 years of art from Egypt in the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam. When the exhibition is over, the objects are taken off their pedestals and packed away, such as a statue of a corn-milling woman, the mummy chest of Dedment and a statue of Merit. Managing Director A. van Schendel comes to watch the proceedings. The objects are then loaded onto a lorry and transported under police escort to Zurich and elsewhere.

Inner coffin of an anonymous lady
desc: Inner chest of anonymous lady ; Painted on stucco (plaster) ; Third Intermediate Period, 21st dynasty (c. 1069-945 BCE) ; Second cachet of Deir el-Bahari (Bab el-Gasous); The inscription at the foot of this casket states that the deceased was a singer of Amon, but her name was left blank. It seems as if the coffin itself was decorated as the Hall of Judgement. Indeed, the rim of the vessel is decorated with a frieze of alternating uraeus (erect cobra) and a Maät feather (symbol of cosmic order). The paintings show how the Amon singer passes the weighing of the heart with flying colours: her heart weighs as much as Maät. Thot (with ibis head) records the result and the deceased, with feathers in her hands, offers herself to the guardians of the afterlife (with snake head). In the afterlife, she is accompanied by her ba (soul bird) as she stands in worship before the tree goddess and the goddess Hathor as cow (protector of the necropolis). The bottom of the vessel depicts the goddess of the west. Accompanying this coffin is a mummy shelf which is in very poor condition (E.5906).r el-Bahari (Bab el-Gasoes) ; The inscription at the foot of this casket states that the deceased was a singer of Amon, but her name was left blank. Αιγυπτιακά ήτοι εξιχνιάσεις περί γεωγραφίας εξ αυτών των ορίων της κατωτέρας Νουβίας μέχρι του κατά Συήνην καταράκτου πρώτου, και εκ τούτου άχρι της Μεσογείου θαλάσσης, περί των εν εκάστη αρχαία πόλει παρά τας δύο όχθας του Νείλου υφισταμένων τεραστίων μνημείων και άλλων ετι θεαμάτων, περί ιερογλύφων, επιγραφών θρησκείας και ιστορίας της τε αρχαιοτέρας και της μετά Αλέξανδρον τον Μέγαν και καθεξής Περικλέους Αιγύπτου

Περιγραφή ιερά του Αγίου και Θεοβαδίστου Ορους Σινά περιέχουσα εν πρώτης μεν την Ακολουθίαν του Αγίου και Ενδόξου Μεγάλου Προφήτου Μωϋσέως του Θεόπτου, δεύτερον δε την Ακολουθίαν της Αγίας Ενδόξου Μεγαλομάρτυρος Χριστονύμφης, Παρθένου και Πανσόφου Αικατερίνης, επομοίως δε εξιστορούσα συντόμως και περιληπτικώς τα του Θεοβαδίστου τούτου Ορους, τούτεσι την θέσιν και Αγιότητα αυτού, τα της βασιλικής λαμπράς οικοδομής του εκείσε περικαλλέστατου μοναστηριού, τα της ερημητών Αράβων, που επισυμνάντας κατά καιρούς μεγάλους κινδίνους τω Αγίω τούτω Μοναστηριών, πάτε είδον αυτού και έξω πέριξ Ιερά προσκυνήματα, μετά τινών θαυμάτων, τους εν αυτώ μέχρι τούτου Αρχιεπίσκοπήσαντας, έτι δε και τους κατά διαφόρους χρόνους επιδημήσαντας εις τούτο το Όρος Αγίους, κι άλλους άνδρας επ' αρετή και μαθήσει διαλάμψαντας, και τελευταίον τω Ακολουθίαν της εν Σινά και Ραιθώ αναιρεθούντων Οσίων Αββάδων, τυπωθείσα νυν πέμπτον δια δαπάνης της Ιεράς και Βασιλικής Μονής του Αγίου και Θεοβαδίστου Ορους Σινά

title: Observații ale unui nespecialist asupra istoriei antice
desc: Volumul cuprinde lecțiile ținute de Nicolae Iorga la "Cercul femeiesc de înnaintare culturală". Acestea sunt lecții de istorie universală antică, de istorie a culturii umane atât a grecilor și romanilor cât și a vechilor civilizații orientale.

title: Aromânii
desc: Lucrarea vorbește despre aromâni care sunt considerați ca fiind cei mai ridicați dintre toți păstorii din jurul Mării Mediterane, ei fiind nu doar păstori ci și mari negustori deoarece această mișcare a lor cu turmele îi ajuta ca la întoarcere să aducă pe cai și catâtri tot felul de mărfuri deoarece aceștia erau tot timpul pe drumuri. Alături de turci, bulgari, sârbi și albanezi, aromânii, pe lângă păstorit, ajunseseră pe o altă treaptă de civilizație și anume burghezia.

title: Stained glass window
desc: Stained glass window in the Church of the Savior in Głotów, province Warmińsko-Mazurskie, depicting Joseph in Egypt. Stained glass made in the studio of Christoph Rings in Cologne in 1877.
credit: The International Center for Information Management Systems and Services

title: Picture on glass - Scarabaeus
desc: Decorative picture painted on glass, imitating stained glass. The 23 x 23 cm image shows Scarabaeus, which was a popular form of amulet in ancient Egypt. Work in progress.

title: 14th century stained glass
desc: The medieval, gothic stained glass window in the cathedral in Włocławek was created around 1360. It consists of 24 quarters, 23 of which are original. 20 sections show biblical scenes. Among the Old Testament representations there are, among others paired prophets Isaac and Abraham, Jeremiah and Ezekiel, Micaiah and Habakkuk, Zechariah and Balaam, kings David and Solomon, Salamiel and Rehoboam, kings of Judah Jehoshaphat and Joram, patriarch Joseph of Egypt and the prophet Malachi, Moses and Jonah, Henoch and Elijah, Daniel and Isaiah. Scenes from the New Testament include Escape from Egypt, Sacrifice in the Temple, Baptism in Jordan, Massacre of the Innocents, Mother of God with Child. In the lancet closures there is Christ's head in the center, and on the sides of the Mother of God and St. Joseph. In the years 1957-1959 the stained glass was thoroughly restored under the supervision of Edward Kwiatkowski and Wiesław Domasłowski. In 2015, the stained glass window underwent another major renovation, which was financed by the Polish-German Foundation. At that time, the gaps were replaced and the cracked glass was glued together, the structure of the stained glass was reinforced with a protective glass and adequate lighting was provided.The Gothic cathedral of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary in Włocławek was built in the years 1340-1411 with later additions.
credit: The International Center for Information Management Systems and Services

title: Zwei blaue Jungen
desc: Kurz nach Ausbruch des Ersten Weltkriegs geraten die deutschen Marinerekruten Hans und Erich in Tunis in französische Kriegsgefangenschaft. Mithilfe eines deutschen Fremdenlegionärs gelingt ihnen die Flucht. Durch die Wüste schlagen sie sich nach Ägypten durch, in dessen Grenzgebiet mit den Deutschen verbündete osmanische Truppen gegen die Briten kämpfen. Ein deutsches Kampfflugzeug rettet Hans und Erich vor den britischen Soldaten und bringt sie nach Konstantinopel, wo sie auf ihr Schiff zurückkehren können. Von "Zwei blaue Jungen", der zum Teil auf dem Schulschiff "Großherzog Friedrich August" entstanden ist und in dem Marinesoldaten als Statisten und in Nebenrollen auftreten, ist nur ein rund fünfminütiges Fragment überliefert, das eine Sequenz vom Ende des Films zeigt.

title: Institution of the Holy Eucharist
desc: O tríptico é proveniente da capela de Santa Marta do Paço Episcopal de Fontelo, em Viseu. Na pintura são identificáveis os processos pictóricos de Vasco Fernandes: a descentralização dos núcleos formais e a sua ordenação em planos sucessivos unificados pela distribuição da luz; o rigor da expressão volumétrica e da forma; a expressividade dos rostos, o preciosismo dos pormenores. A importância desta obra passa também pela complexidade iconográfica e pela relação entre a narrativa, desenvolvida de modo contínuo, e a forma tripartida. Na tábua central representa-se a Última Ceia: Jesus Cristo, que segura o cálice eucarístico, é ladeado por São Pedro, São João e um outro apóstolo. Na tábua da esquerda, sete apóstolos organizados em redor da mesa, prolongada da tábua central com a forma de L, elevam a hóstia eucarística. Judas, na tábua da direita, com os elementos iconográficos alusivos à traição (o saco de moedas e o traje amarelo), ainda está no grupo. As representações nesta tábua direita, para além de Judas e do cão (símbolo da fidelidade oposta à traição), são invulgares. O episódio do Lava-pés é evocado através da presença de um menino junto da bacia com água em primeiro plano, e as duas figuras femininas que se aproximam de Cristo, uma das quais segura a boceta com perfume, atributo de Maria Madalena, aludindo à dicotomia entre o Amor Profano e o Amor Sagrado. A unidade visual é criada por um muro contínuo que separa os planos. Na tábua central, assomam de um compartimento contíguo algumas personagens, uma das quais transporta para a mesa eucarística o cordeiro, de acordo com a celebração da páscoa judaica. Os elementos dispostos sobre a mesa, as ervas amargas e o pão ázimo, aludem ao tema da Saída do Egipto. Nos dois fundos restantes evocam-se as cenas sequentes da Paixão (autor do texto – Maria João Vilhena).
credit: National Museum of Grao Vasco, Viseu
